_comment: A routing infantry block rallies at full flight and its men pull up from the run on their own rather than stopping dead. Team 0's 72-man Infantry block spawns ALREADY routing (starting_state 3) facing north, its own back edge, so each man flees straight ahead; drill mode, so no enemy is ever near and the rally only waits on its morale. Morale 15 is staged so the men have built up to their full flee pace (104 wu/s, 1.3 x the 80 wu/s sprint) when the recovering morale crosses the rally threshold at tick 263 or 264 (60 Hz dump basis; IDLE on the tick-264 sample), with the men's centroid at y 1390.7. Each man then slows along his own run at his braking rate (SoldierBodies.pull_up_rallied), and the unit re-forms where they come to rest. The unit's position reads the men's centroid while they pull up, so the two position expects show the halt: y 1339.96 at tick 300 (pinned at 1337.0, within its 5 wu tol) and y 1286.34 at tick 420, about 104 wu past the rally, identical on seeds 0 to 4 (dense 2-tick FULL dumps, measured 2026-11-13 on #1949's branch). A rally that stopped the men dead would read y 1390.7 at both ticks. The tick-420 pin was y 1295.8 for the old flight's anchor, which braked as one at the Infantry decel; the bottom-up flight (#1949) removed it, and the men's own pull-up carries the centroid 9.5 wu further. The current_speed pin (68.0 at tick 300) is retired: a unit whose men pull up on their own has no pace of its own to read (it reads 0.0), and the position pins carry the claim. Flat declared map (terrain empty). The camera follows the flight and holds over the halt. Driven live through tools/demo/DemoInputRecorder.gd (no player input: the rout and the rally are the sim's own); world coordinates; physics ticks (60/s).
